objective.statement: Optional: understand music that begins before the first bar-line.
successCriteria: I know a piece can start with an upbeat before the first bar-line.
I know the upbeat and the last bar together make one whole bar.
I know this lesson is optional and is not in the Grade 3 assessment.

explanation.text: This lesson is optional. It helps you read music, but you do not need it to complete Grade 3, and nothing in it is in the Grade 3 assessment.
Many tunes begin with a note, or a few notes, before the first bar-line. This is called an upbeat, or an anacrusis. The first full bar starts after the upbeat.

music.textAlternative: An upbeat of one crotchet, then a full bar of two minims, then a last bar of a minim and a crotchet.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: crotchet. Bar 2: minim, minim. Bar 3: minim, crotchet.

explanation.caption: An upbeat of one crotchet. The first full bar begins after it.

explanation.text: Because the piece starts part-way through a bar, the last bar is usually shorter than the others. The upbeat and the last bar together add up to one whole bar. A piece in 3/4 that starts with one crotchet upbeat can end with a last bar of two crotchets.
Whatever the length of the upbeat, group its notes as though they were the end of a bar. The last bar is grouped in the usual way, up to the point where the music stops.
Upbeat + last bar = one whole bar.

music.textAlternative: An upbeat of one crotchet, a bar of two minims and a short last bar.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: crotchet. Bar 2: minim, minim. Bar 3: minim, crotchet.

steps: Count one crotchet beat for the upbeat before the first bar-line.
The full bar that follows has the length of the time signature.
The last bar is one crotchet short. Together with the upbeat it makes one whole bar.
demonstration.textAlternative: A crotchet upbeat, a full bar of two minims and a last bar of a minim and a crotchet.

guided.prompt: A tune starts with one crotchet before the first bar-line. What is this called?

tie.reason: A tie joins two notes of the same pitch. A note before the first bar-line is an upbeat.

triplet.reason: A triplet is a group of three notes in a beat. A note before the first bar-line is an upbeat.

pause.reason: A pause holds a note longer. A note before the first bar-line is an upbeat.

hints: The upbeat and the last bar together make one whole bar.

mistakes.evidence-misread: A pause holds a note longer. A note before the first bar-line is an upbeat.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. This lesson is optional, so take your time: the opening upbeat and the last bar together add up to one full bar.

guided.prompt: A piece in 3/4 starts with an upbeat of one crotchet. How many crotchet beats are in its last bar?

1.reason: One crotchet plus one crotchet is only two beats. A bar of 3/4 needs three, so the last bar has two.

3.reason: Three beats would be a whole bar on its own. The upbeat already supplies one of them.

hints: The upbeat and the last bar together make one whole bar.

feedback.correct: Yes: one beat of upbeat plus two beats make a whole bar of three.

mistakes.evidence-misread: Three beats would be a whole bar on its own. The upbeat already supplies one of them.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. This lesson is optional, so take your time: the opening upbeat and the last bar together add up to one full bar.

independent.prompt: A piece in 4/4 starts with an upbeat of one crotchet. How many crotchet beats are in its last bar?

2.reason: One plus two is only three beats. A bar of 4/4 needs four, so the last bar has three.

4.reason: Four beats would be a whole bar on its own.

hints: The upbeat and the last bar together make one whole bar.

feedback.correct: Right: one plus three makes four.

mistakes.evidence-misread: Four beats would be a whole bar on its own.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. This lesson is optional, so take your time: the opening upbeat and the last bar together add up to one full bar.

independent.prompt: A piece in 2/4 starts with an upbeat of one quaver. How many quavers are in its last bar? (A bar of 2/4 holds four quavers.)

2.reason: One plus two is only three quavers. A bar of 2/4 holds four.

4.reason: Four quavers would be a whole bar on its own.

hints: The upbeat and the last bar together make one whole bar.

feedback.correct: Right: one quaver plus three quavers make a whole bar of four.

mistakes.evidence-misread: Four quavers would be a whole bar on its own.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. This lesson is optional, so take your time: the opening upbeat and the last bar together add up to one full bar.

independent.prompt: A piece in 6/8 starts with an upbeat of one quaver. How many quavers are in its last bar? (A bar of 6/8 holds six quavers.)

3.reason: One plus three is only four quavers. A bar of 6/8 holds six.

6.reason: Six quavers would be a whole bar on its own.

hints: The upbeat and the last bar together make one whole bar.

feedback.correct: Right: one plus five makes six.

mistakes.evidence-misread: Six quavers would be a whole bar on its own.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. This lesson is optional, so take your time: the opening upbeat and the last bar together add up to one full bar.

independent.prompt: A piece in 4/4 starts with an upbeat of two quavers. How many crotchet beats are in its last bar? (Two quavers last one crotchet.)

2.reason: One beat of upbeat plus two is only three beats. A bar of 4/4 needs four, so the last bar has three.

4.reason: Four beats would be a whole bar on its own.

hints: The upbeat and the last bar together make one whole bar.

feedback.correct: Right: the upbeat is one beat, so the last bar holds three.

mistakes.evidence-misread: Four beats would be a whole bar on its own.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. This lesson is optional, so take your time: the opening upbeat and the last bar together add up to one full bar.

recap: An upbeat is a note or notes before the first bar-line.
The upbeat and the last bar together make one whole bar.
